hyps.why: At very small learning rates training underconverges in 243 epochs, so increasing the step size gives large gains.
At already large learning rates Adam becomes unstable, so increasing further causes divergence and accuracy loss.
Large batches give fewer, less noisy updates, so they tolerate and benefit more from larger learning rates.
With a tiny learning rate, fewer updates per epoch from larger batches worsens underconvergence.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, partially stabilizing training at aggressive learning rates.
When L2 penalty is already strong, increasing it further causes severe underfitting.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so adding units helps much more than at large widths.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence and dead units under large learning rates.
Reducing an unstable, too-large learning rate restores training and improves accuracy.
Relaxing an excessive L2 penalty relieves underfitting, whereas lowering an already tiny alpha does little.
